questions.questionText: Mara reread the message, placed her phone face down, and continued stirring a cup she had not tasted. What can most reasonably be inferred?
options: The message has unsettled or distracted Mara
Mara dislikes all hot drinks
The phone battery has run out
Mara is waiting for several dinner guests to arrive
questions.correctAnswer: The message has unsettled or distracted Mara
questions.explanation: Her repeated reading and absent-minded stirring support emotional distraction; the other claims are not supported by the details.

curriculum.objective: Develop defensible interpretations of complex texts by selecting precise evidence and distinguishing inference from explicit meaning.

questions.questionText: A narrator calls the new policy “a remarkably elegant solution—provided nobody asks whom it excludes.” What attitude is conveyed?
options: Unqualified admiration
Sceptical irony
Nostalgic regret
Complete indifference
questions.correctAnswer: Sceptical irony
questions.explanation: The initial praise is undercut by the condition about exclusion, creating an ironic and critical attitude toward the policy.

curriculum.objective: Develop defensible interpretations of complex texts by selecting precise evidence and distinguishing inference from explicit meaning.

questions.questionText: Which quotation best supports the inference that the town’s apparent calm is fragile?
options: The square had been carefully repaved during the previous summer.
At noon, the bakery opened its striped awning.
Every conversation stopped when the siren was tested.
A bicycle leaned beside the library steps.
questions.correctAnswer: Every conversation stopped when the siren was tested.
questions.explanation: The sudden collective silence suggests underlying anxiety, making it stronger evidence of fragile calm than neutral setting details.

curriculum.objective: Develop defensible interpretations of complex texts by selecting precise evidence and distinguishing inference from explicit meaning.

questions.questionText: A speaker insists, “I mention the award only because accuracy matters,” then refers to it three more times. Which interpretation is best supported?
options: The speaker has forgotten receiving the award
The speaker doubts that the award exists
The speaker wants the audience to ignore status
The speaker is self-promoting while denying that intention
questions.correctAnswer: The speaker is self-promoting while denying that intention
questions.explanation: Repeatedly mentioning the award conflicts with the stated motive, revealing self-promotion through the gap between claim and behaviour.

curriculum.objective: Develop defensible interpretations of complex texts by selecting precise evidence and distinguishing inference from explicit meaning.

questions.questionText: In the phrase “the deadline crept closer,” what effect does the verb “crept” create?
options: It suggests a slow but threatening approach
It proves that the deadline was officially rescheduled
It makes the deadline sound cheerful
It describes a literal animal
questions.correctAnswer: It suggests a slow but threatening approach
questions.explanation: The personifying verb implies quiet, gradual movement and gives the approaching deadline a threatening quality.

curriculum.objective: Analyse how diction, imagery, syntax and structural choices shape meaning, tone and reader response.

questions.questionText: A paragraph describing a storm begins with long sentences but ends: “Then silence.” What is the main structural effect?
options: It introduces a new narrator
It creates an abrupt contrast after sustained movement
It proves the storm lasted only seconds
It changes the text into a formal report
questions.correctAnswer: It creates an abrupt contrast after sustained movement
questions.explanation: The short final sentence breaks the earlier rhythm, making the sudden silence feel sharp and emphatic.

curriculum.objective: Analyse how diction, imagery, syntax and structural choices shape meaning, tone and reader response.

questions.questionText: Why might a writer repeat the opening phrase “We were told” at the start of several consecutive sentences?
options: To avoid using any punctuation
To make every sentence the same length
To emphasise a pattern of imposed claims
To show that events occur in alphabetical order
questions.correctAnswer: To emphasise a pattern of imposed claims
questions.explanation: The anaphora foregrounds repeated messages from an authority and can build a critical sense of pressure or manipulation.

curriculum.objective: Analyse how diction, imagery, syntax and structural choices shape meaning, tone and reader response.

questions.questionText: A story reveals its final event first, then returns to the previous morning. What is the most likely effect of this structure?
options: It removes all uncertainty from the story
It prevents readers from comparing causes
It makes chronology impossible to follow
It shifts suspense from what happens to how and why it happens
questions.correctAnswer: It shifts suspense from what happens to how and why it happens
questions.explanation: Knowing the outcome redirects attention toward causation, motive and the sequence of choices leading to the revealed event.

curriculum.objective: Analyse how diction, imagery, syntax and structural choices shape meaning, tone and reader response.

questions.questionText: Which statement is a claim rather than evidence?
options: The new timetable will improve student wellbeing
The survey included a sample of 420 enrolled students
Attendance rose by 3% last term
The report was published in May
questions.correctAnswer: The new timetable will improve student wellbeing
questions.explanation: It asserts a predicted benefit that requires support, while the other choices present checkable factual information.

curriculum.objective: Evaluate claims, evidence, assumptions and source reliability in informational and argumentative texts.

questions.questionText: An article about a supplement cites only testimonials from customers selected by the manufacturer. What is the strongest concern?
options: The article uses complete sentences
The evidence may be selectively chosen and lacks independent testing
Customers are never allowed to discuss products
Testimonials always contain numerical errors
questions.correctAnswer: The evidence may be selectively chosen and lacks independent testing
questions.explanation: Manufacturer-selected testimonials create selection bias and do not provide controlled, independent evidence of effectiveness.

curriculum.objective: Evaluate claims, evidence, assumptions and source reliability in informational and argumentative texts.

questions.questionText: “Two top athletes use this training app, so it will make every user elite.” Which flaw is most evident?
options: It defines all technical terms
It compares two identical datasets
It generalises from exceptional examples and assumes causation
It presents too many independent trials
questions.correctAnswer: It generalises from exceptional examples and assumes causation
questions.explanation: The claim treats unusual cases as representative and assumes the app caused their success without controlling other factors.

curriculum.objective: Evaluate claims, evidence, assumptions and source reliability in informational and argumentative texts.

questions.questionText: A transport study reports a 20% fall in delays after a route change but gives no seasonal comparison. Which additional evidence would best test the claimed effect?
options: A photograph of the new route signs
The project manager’s opinion of the change
A list of all vehicle colours
Delay data from comparable months before and after the change
questions.correctAnswer: Delay data from comparable months before and after the change
questions.explanation: Comparing equivalent periods helps separate the route change from seasonal variation and provides a more credible basis for causal inference.

curriculum.objective: Evaluate claims, evidence, assumptions and source reliability in informational and argumentative texts.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses subject–verb agreement correctly?
options: The collection of essays is on the desk.
The collection of essays are on the desk.
The essays in the collection is revised.
The collection have been on the desk.
questions.correctAnswer: The collection of essays is on the desk.
questions.explanation: The head noun “collection” is singular, so it takes the singular verb “is” despite the plural noun in the prepositional phrase.

curriculum.objective: Apply accurate grammar, punctuation and cohesive devices to create controlled, unambiguous extended writing.

questions.questionText: Which revision fixes the ambiguous pronoun in “When Lena called Priya, she was leaving the station”?
options: When Lena called Priya, she left.
As Priya was leaving the station, Lena called her.
Lena called Priya because she was there.
When she called her, Priya left the station.
questions.correctAnswer: As Priya was leaving the station, Lena called her.
questions.explanation: Naming Priya as the person leaving removes uncertainty about which woman the original pronoun “she” refers to.

curriculum.objective: Apply accurate grammar, punctuation and cohesive devices to create controlled, unambiguous extended writing.

questions.questionText: Which connector best completes the reasoning? “The sample was small; _____, the findings should be treated as preliminary.”
options: for example
similarly
therefore
meanwhile
questions.correctAnswer: therefore
questions.explanation: The second clause is a consequence of the small sample, so the result connector “therefore” makes the relationship explicit.

curriculum.objective: Apply accurate grammar, punctuation and cohesive devices to create controlled, unambiguous extended writing.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses punctuation to integrate the explanation most effectively?
options: The proposal failed, its costs were unclear.
The proposal failed because: its costs were unclear.
The proposal failed; because its costs were unclear.
The proposal failed for one reason: its costs were unclear.
questions.correctAnswer: The proposal failed for one reason: its costs were unclear.
questions.explanation: A complete clause introduces a specific explanation after the colon; the other choices create a comma splice or misuse the colon or semicolon.

curriculum.subskill: Introduce an explanation with a colon
curriculum.objective: Apply accurate grammar, punctuation and cohesive devices to create controlled, unambiguous extended writing.

questions.questionText: Which opening is most appropriate for a formal email requesting information from a university department?
options: Dear Admissions Officer, I am writing to ask about the application timetable.
Hey there! Tell me when applications happen.
Applications—what is going on with those?
Yo, I need the dates as soon as possible.
questions.correctAnswer: Dear Admissions Officer, I am writing to ask about the application timetable.
questions.explanation: The greeting, complete sentence and courteous direct request suit a formal institutional audience.

curriculum.objective: Adapt register, organisation and rhetorical choices to communicate effectively for a specified purpose, audience and form.

questions.questionText: A safety leaflet is intended for first-time visitors to a climbing centre. Which feature would most improve usability?
options: A long history of the building
Numbered actions with clear imperative verbs
Technical terms without definitions
A single dense paragraph in small type
questions.correctAnswer: Numbered actions with clear imperative verbs
questions.explanation: New visitors need instructions they can scan and follow quickly, so ordered steps and direct verbs serve the practical purpose.

curriculum.objective: Adapt register, organisation and rhetorical choices to communicate effectively for a specified purpose, audience and form.

questions.questionText: Which sentence best suits a balanced editorial about extending the school day?
options: Only a fool could support this terrible idea.
Longer days are perfect and have no drawbacks.
Additional time may broaden activities, but costs and student fatigue require careful consideration.
The timetable exists, and timetables contain hours.
questions.correctAnswer: Additional time may broaden activities, but costs and student fatigue require careful consideration.
questions.explanation: The sentence acknowledges a possible benefit and relevant drawbacks, matching the measured register and purpose of a balanced editorial.

curriculum.objective: Adapt register, organisation and rhetorical choices to communicate effectively for a specified purpose, audience and form.

questions.questionText: A charity wants young adults to volunteer for a weekend river clean-up. Which approach best combines credibility and motivation?
options: Promise that one weekend will permanently solve pollution
Use guilt without explaining the activity
List regulations in legal language only
Give verified local impact data, a clear role description and a direct sign-up link
questions.correctAnswer: Give verified local impact data, a clear role description and a direct sign-up link
questions.explanation: Evidence builds trust, practical detail reduces uncertainty, and a clear action makes the persuasive purpose easy for the audience to fulfil.

curriculum.subskill: Combine evidence and call to action
curriculum.objective: Adapt register, organisation and rhetorical choices to communicate effectively for a specified purpose, audience and form.
